2588: Kaneda is a carefree gang-leader who boasts a custom-modified motorcycle. He and Tetsuo have been best friends since early childhood. He is brash and not above teasing Tetsuo despite feeling affection for him as a younger brother.
2589: Kaneda's best friend since preschool and the second principal subject of the story's theme. Tetsuo is shown as a black sheep in the gang he and Kaneda are part of, and quietly suffers from a deeply rooted inferiority complex.
9875: A young woman whom Kaneda meets on his quest to find Tetsuo. She is a member of an anti-government organization that Ryu and Nezu are also involved in. Kei's role in the Resistance is important because she is completely loyal to its cause and to Ryu.
16288: A senior military officer who oversees research into psychic abilities. He listens closely to the three Esper children, and seeks to capture Tetsuo to exploit his powers.
16289: A timid young girl who ends up becoming Tetsuo's companion and Akira's babysitter.
20463: One of the most prominent members of Kaneda's gang. He often derides Tetsuo, which leads to harsh feelings between them that will ultimately seal his fate. (Credit to Wikipedia)
24735: Codename #28 in the Japanese government's secret ESP project. An estimately 8 year old boy around whom the story revolves.
28166: Sometimes known as Kaisuke, he is a high-ranking member of Kaneda's gang. He does not play a major role at first​ but becomes more prominent later in the story.
142837: Ryuusaku is a comrade of Kei's in the resistance movement who claims to be Kei's brother, but it is implied that this is not the case.
142838: Nezu was a parliament member who is also the leader of the terrorist resistance movement against the government.
142840: Lady Miyako was a former test subject known as "Designated #19" from the Project. She is the high priestess and leader of a temple in Neo-Tokyo and a major ally of Kaneda and Kei as the story progresses, who plays an important role in the final battle with Tetsuo Shima.
